question.text: The change in the magnitude of the volume of an ideal gas when a small additional pressure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> is applied at a constant temperature, is the same as the change when the temperature is reduced by a small quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>∆</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> at constant pressure. The initial temperature and pressure of the gas were <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo> </mo></math>and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi></math> respectively. If  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>|</mo><mi>ΔT</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>|</mo><mi>ΔP</mi><mo>|</mo></math> then value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>atm</mi><mo>)</mo></math>  is __________

solution.text:
PV=nRT

PΔV+VΔP=0

ΔV=-ΔPPV  ....(i)

  In second case

PΔV=-nRΔT

ΔV=-nRΔTP    ...(ii)

equating (i) and (ii)

nRΔTP=-ΔPPV

ΔT=ΔP VnR

c=vnR

Putting the value of V, n and  R , C = 150
